diagram_math_checks.result: Choose U′ open in X′ with ψ:U′→X×A^n étale and φ|U′=πψ as in F1 and step 3.1. U′_i=U′×_X X_i. The map ψ_i:U′_i→X_i×A^n is the base change of ψ along X_i×A^n→X×A^n; π_i:X_i×A^n→X_i is projection, so their composite is the restriction of φ_i.

diagram_math_checks.check: Vertical maps, commutativity and Cartesian relations
diagram_math_checks.result: σ_{i+1}:X_{i+1}→X_i is a specified original blowup stage; its product is σ_{i+1}×1. τ_{i+1}:U′_{i+1}→U′_i is the induced fibre-product map. The right square is the base change of σ along π_i. Associativity of fibre products identifies the left upper node with U′_i×_(X_i×A^n)(X_{i+1}×A^n), proving the left square Cartesian as well. Thus (σ×1)ψ_{i+1}=ψ_iτ_{i+1} and σπ_{i+1}=π_i(σ×1).

For C_i⊂X_i the product center is C_i×A^n by step 2.1. Its inverse under ψ_i is U′_i×_(X_i)C_i. F2 and the actual smooth-base-change supplier Statement and proof 1.2 identify τ with this center’s blowup when nonempty. Empty inverse centers yield inserted isomorphisms. The multiple-test-blowup definition and étale maximal-order supplier proof 4.1 require retaining nonempty Cartier centers even when the underlying blowup map is an isomorphism.

Step 2.1 identifies the projection sequence with products; step 3.1 and actual canonical-resolution proposition proof 8.1 identify the étale-pulled-back sequence only up to extension. The final paragraph keeps original stage indices, omits only empty-center steps in the canonical comparison and retains nonempty centers. Invariant equalities are stated only on supports at corresponding stages. No additional uniqueness, global factorization, or isomorphism of unaligned canonical sequences is asserted.
